questions.prompt: Which mental model best explains “Source Maps” in Dart Sass?
options: The browser executes Sass source directly, so a compilation step is unnecessary.
Readable SCSS guarantees correct browser rendering, accessibility, and performance without output review.
The best solution is always to replace native CSS behavior with a new Sass abstraction.

Treat the toolchain as a repeatable pipeline: keep editable SCSS as input, let Dart Sass compile an explicit entrypoint, and inspect the generated CSS or map. Separate local setup problems from errors in the stylesheet itself.
questions.answer_key: Treat the toolchain as a repeatable pipeline: keep editable SCSS as input, let Dart Sass compile an explicit entrypoint, and inspect the generated CSS or map. Separate local setup problems from errors in the stylesheet itself.
questions.explanation: Treat the toolchain as a repeatable pipeline: keep editable SCSS as input, let Dart Sass compile an explicit entrypoint, and inspect the generated CSS or map. Separate local setup problems from errors in the stylesheet itself. The alternative choices confuse Sass compilation with browser execution or claim guarantees that require independent tests.

questions.prompt: When applying “What source maps are”, which approach is the most reliable?
options: Prefer deeply nested selectors because fewer source lines always mean simpler and safer CSS.
Silence every warning before determining whether it identifies a deprecated or incorrect construct.
Identify the collection, the per-item rule, and the stopping condition. Validate collection shape and inspect the count and naming of generated rules.
Skip compilation and infer the final selector list and property values from the source file alone.
questions.answer_key: Identify the collection, the per-item rule, and the stopping condition. Validate collection shape and inspect the count and naming of generated rules.
questions.explanation: Identify the collection, the per-item rule, and the stopping condition. Validate collection shape and inspect the count and naming of generated rules. Compare the compiled output with the stated intent and preserve browser-native behavior where it is required.

questions.prompt: Which review decision most directly supports maintainability for “Source Maps”?
options: Expose internal implementation details as public API and postpone documentation until after release.

A reliable workflow gives every teammate the same command and an observable output. Commit source and scripts; decide deliberately whether generated CSS and source maps belong in the repository or are build artifacts.
Generate every possible selector or theme combination, even when most variants are never used.
Treat successful compilation as proof that the interface is accessible and behaves correctly in every browser.
questions.answer_key: A reliable workflow gives every teammate the same command and an observable output. Commit source and scripts; decide deliberately whether generated CSS and source maps belong in the repository or are build artifacts.
questions.explanation: A reliable workflow gives every teammate the same command and an observable output. Commit source and scripts; decide deliberately whether generated CSS and source maps belong in the repository or are build artifacts. The other choices increase output, assume unverified behavior, or make the public interface harder to maintain.
